lines.text:
“You did read

“Errm...

case brief?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR

“You’re telling me

“Oh, that case brief.

lines.text:
“It’s a long walk
back, though.

Maybe I can just
borrow yours?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“The office copy
is in the case-file cabinet.

It is available
on a need-to-know basis...

and without an approved
authorization form...

there is nothing

lines.speaker: ARTHUR

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “Pay attention.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Fully focused.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Starting now.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“This is going
to be a long day.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Euler Finance
was hacked.

A large amount
of digital assets
was taken.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Any witnesses?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “No.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Any suspects?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Not one
we can identify
from the record.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Crime scene?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“The transactions
are the crime scene.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“That sounds
inconveniently abstract.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“All we have
is the public record
of those transactions.

The blockchain.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “The block...what?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“The BLOCKCHAIN.

A public ledger.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“It records
what moved...

when it moved...

and which wallet addresses
sent and received it.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Once recorded,
those entries cannot
simply be erased.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“So whoever did this
left a trail.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “Yes.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Great.

This already sounds
like a closed case to me.

We just go to
this public chain thingy...

and trace the activity.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“*Public* is not
the same as *simple*.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“The ledger is enormous...

technical...

and full of activity
that has nothing
to do with this case.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“It’s like trying
to find a needle

in a mathematically
precise haystack.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Sounds complicated.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “It is.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Fortunately,
our office has been authorized
to use the Nansen API
for this case.

The case terminal
already has
the relevant records loaded.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Nansen helps us organize
and query the activity...

sort through the noise...

and surface patterns
or relationships

that would be difficult
to spot manually.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“So Nansen
solves the case.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“No.

Nansen has organized
the activity.

It has not decided
which activity matters.

That is where
you come in.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “So I need a clue.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “You need a question.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “I have several.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “One *relevant* question.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“So then,
just hand over
the terminal access...

and I’ll get started.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Our office
is authorized
to use the Nansen API
for this case.

You are not authorized
to use the case terminal.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“But I’m
the lead investigator.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“The more
you remind me of that...

the worse
my migraine gets.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“It does not matter
who you are.

You need to submit
a terminal authorization form.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“It must pass through
the appropriate
management channels...

and receive approval
from the shift manager.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Who’s the shift manager?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “I am.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“So the management channel
is you.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “It is company policy.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Where do I get
the form?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Take a blank
terminal authorization form
from the dispenser...

fill it out...

and bring it back to me.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Until you submit it...

and unless management
renders you
a favorable response...

do not use
the terminal...

do not access
the case files...

and do not touch
anything else.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“A bulky machine
for storing,
printing,
and dispensing
office forms.

It’s basically
a printer...

with more authority.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Signed
and ready for Mr. A.

And once he approves it...

I can finally access
the terminal

and the case files.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“The nib is cracked.

The feather is bent.

It gave everything
it had

to corporate
authorization.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“I could totally
lift that.

Any other day.

Yesterday was leg day.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Please make sure
to give that back
when you’re done.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Nope.

It weighs more
than it looks...

and it already
looks enormous.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“That is one thing
I’m man enough
to admit

I am absolutely
not authorized
to open.

I don’t need
a rejected form
to tell me that.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“It’s already shut.

And fastened
with proprietary screws

that require
an exorbitantly priced
manufacturer-approved
screwdriver.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“It already printed
the form I need.

Any more paperwork
and this becomes
a desk job.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Bureaucratic office forms.

My favorite.

Nothing says
‘urgent investigation’...

like stopping
to fill one out.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“A feather pen.

Elegant.

I wonder how
the bird feels...

knowing one
of its feathers

ended up supporting
tedious office management.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Name.

Role.

Reason for access.

Signature.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Very official.

These guys
don’t mess around.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Fancy feather.

Sharp,
inked-up,
little nib.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “It’s blank.”

be laughing?”

before this day

my lips on that.”

Stamped.

Fully authorized.

And apparently
the dinosaurs were acceptable
for the signature field.”

lines.text:
“A rubber band.

Currently performing
its traditional role...

taking up space
until the exact moment
someone throws it away
and immediately needs one.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Still scrambled.

I could solve it...

if I knew how
and had several
uninterrupted years.”

lines.text:
“Sharknado 2.

On VHS.

I’m surprised
the first one got made.

I’m even more surprised
someone green-lit
a sequel...

and then preserved it
on obsolete plastic.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“I heard a rumor
the leading shark

was played
by Bruce’s nephew.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“I’m watching this
when I get home.

Right after I find
an antique store

willing to admit
it still sells VCRs.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Wow.

This thing
has some weight to it.

Properly heavy-duty.

I might actually need
to be careful with this.

I feel like
I could accidentally
break something.”

lines.text:
“Small.

Dainty.

Very pointy.

Perfect for hanging
my keys by the door...

or the calendar
I’ve been meaning
to put up all year.

It’s already December...

but better late
than never.

The possibilities
are endless!”

“Euler Finance.

lines.text:
“DAI.

A stablecoin built
to stay close
to the dollar.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“The first DAI entry records
just over 8,877,507 DAI—

about $8.8 million
at the time.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“The wider exploit reached
roughly $197 million

across several assets.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Now I have:

the exact token,
the amount,
and the contract address.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Time to trace
the transactions.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“The first transaction
led to the First Engine.

That’s the start
of the trail...

not the end.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“The First Engine.

The Receiving Vault.

And one missing link
between them.

I need the exact transaction
that tells me
whether they actually connect.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“The exact transaction
connects the routes.

Now I need to line up
the amount...

the receiver...

and the link...

and lock the proof
in place.”

Receiver.

Link.

to close the case.”

“I don’t think
stretching a rubber band
around that

improves anything.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Not seeing
a combination here.

On the cube...

or otherwise.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“I feel like
using the hammer
on that

would create
more paperwork.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“That does not need
a tiny,
permanent hole in it.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Whatever is inside...

that is not
getting it out.”

lines.text:
“The terminal
investigates crimes.

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“It doesn’t look like
that can play
VHS tapes...

which may be
the first piece
of good news today.”

lines.text:
“Do-It-Herself.

Small.

Pink.

Radiating competence.

This toolbox believes
I can repair things
without supervision.

That makes one of us.

Still...

I admire its confidence.”

Let’s see what kind
of professional-grade
responsibility
is in here.”

lines.text:
“A hammer.

A small handful
of dainty nails.

And an empty spot
where it looks like

a screwdriver
was supposed to be.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“So...

a hammer...

a handful of nails...

a screwdriver-shaped vacancy...

and one newly
self-certified handyman.

Look out,
property values.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Empty now.

Still pink.

Still empowering.

And, by default...

the most organized
toolbox I’ve ever owned.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Closed tight.

The little pink plastic clips
snapped right into place.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Alright, piggy.

One financial question.

Is Bitcoin
about to pump...

or dump?”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Oink?”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Oink oinkity
oink oink?”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Fine.

I have Nansen access
anyways...

Some help
you were, piggy.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Sorry, little pig.

This might sting
a little.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“One gentle tap.

Just enough
to take a tiny chip
out of the bottom.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“...I was aiming
for one chip.”

underestimated

lines.text:

888,888,888.’”

eight hundred eighty-eight.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “Arthur!”

lines.text: “Mr. A!”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “I’m RICH!”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text: “No.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“You answered that
alarmingly fast.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Token quantity
is not value.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“There are nine
WHOLE digits.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“And not one of them
tells you

what a single token
is worth.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text: “I don’t believe you.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“You don’t have to.

Use Token God Mode
on the Nansen terminal.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“Check the price,
the liquidity,
who’s buying and selling...

and whether any real value
is flowing in or out.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Or confirm
that I’m independently wealthy.”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“I wouldn’t hold
your breath over it.”

lines.text:
“Fine.

I’ll check it myself.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Bitcoin Roller Coaster Guy.

Eight hundred eighty-eight million
BRCG.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“There are still
nine whole digits.

That *feels* rich.

I need to check this out
for myself
in the terminal.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“Eight hundred eighty-eight million BRCG.

About $7.10
at the snapshot’s price.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“That’s a lot of digits
doing very little work.”

lines.text:

isn’t worth
the paper it’s printed on.

the paper might be
the strongest asset.

Somewhere,
the U.S. dollar
is taking notes.”

lines.speaker: ROOK
lines.text:
“I don’t want
to damage it.

It might be
worth something.

I should check
the terminal.”

lines.speaker: ROOK

“I don’t want
to damage it.

BRCG could pump
someday.

Then who’ll
be laughing?”

lines.speaker: ROOK

“I think I’ll hold onto

our budding

handing over
a lottery ticket...

without checking
the winning numbers.”

lines.text:
“I have a feeling

I’ll hold onto it.”

lines.text:
“I don’t think
he’d want that.”

lines.text:
“What should I be
doing right now?”

the Euler file.

lines.text: “What’s next?”

lines.text:
“Use the Nansen terminal.

from the Euler file.”

lines.text:
“The token,

lines.text: “And a relevant question.”

lines.text:
“What should I
follow next?”

lines.speaker: ARTHUR
lines.text:
“You found
where the DAI landed.

where it moved afterward.”

lines.text:
“I have
a few possible readings.”

“Then identify
the one exact record

whether the routes connect.”

“I found

the receiver...

and the link.”

lines.text:
“I think I might have
the case details
all figured out.”

lines.text:
“I don’t think anyone
would blame me
for being skeptical.

close the case
in the terminal.”

and queries
blockchain activity...

filters the noise...

and surfaces
useful patterns.”

lines.text:
“And I ask
the right question.”

“I was hoping
